items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: he come over and said, 'Come on in -- maybe you could join the tail end of the show and see what you can do.'

ctx.x: And after he came back from singing he says, "I'm gonna be a big star one of these days. This is my last week, and I'm going with Tommy Dorsey." And I was amazed that he'd even talk to me, you know. Like I said, I was just a kid, and being on the South Side, you didn't fraternize too much with the white people, you know.

I'll never forget it, though, he gave me a picture -- I lost that picture back in 1955; somebody stole my belongings, because I had messed up; if they didn't steal them then I left them there, never did find them misplaced them. But I moved out of this room, -- but I remember that; we went out that night, and oh my God, we played, we sang "The Lamp is Low" -- I'll never forget the routine we did. "The Lamp is Low" -- we did "The Sheik of Arabee" and we closed with "Tiger Rag" which we used as a flash, and we…

Jerry was managing Harry James, and he said, 'Well, you got to sign these options. We're gonna take you out to Victor Hugo's out in the West Coast.' He says, 'We're gonna give you a couple of jobs playing up there -- at the Hotel Sherman -- for smokers.' However, we signed these options and we went down there a couple of times; they had a couple of jobs while the band was still there.
